entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 1  Dated this the 10th day of June, 2025  ORDER
This bail application is filed under section 482 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short 'BNSS').
2. Petitioner is the accused in Crime No.438 of 2025 of Ernakulam Central Police Station, registered for the offence punishable under Sections 406 and 420 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.

3. According to the defacto complainant, the accused, who is allegedly conducting an online trading establishment by name 'Algora Management Trading Company', induced the defacto complainant to deposit an amount of Rs.9,75,000/-.
After transfer of the said amount, the defacto complainant's account was purposely locked out, resulting in loss of the entire amount and thereby the accused committed the offences alleged.

4. I have heard Sri. Binu V. V., the learned counsel for the petitioner as well as Sri. Noushad K. A.,
the learned Public Prosecutor.
5. The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the entire prosecution allegations are false and the incident as alleged had not occurred.

It was also submitted that a reading of the FI Statement indicates that petitioner had never induced the defacto complainant to 2025:KER:40997 invest any money in the establishment run by the petitioner, and on the other hand, it is evident that even before becoming acquainted with the petitioner the defacto complainant had commenced investment in share trading, and therefore, petitioner cannot be said to have committed the offences alleged.
6.

The learned Public Prosecutor, on the other hand, submitted that the allegations require custodial interrogation of the petitioner, as they are serious, and only such an interrogation would reveal the intricacies of online fraud perpetrated by the petitioner.

7. On a consideration of the rival contentions, this Court notices that the petitioner is alleged to have induced the defacto complainant to deposit amounts in an online trading platform and thereafter locked out the defacto complainant without returning any amounts.
8. The nature of allegations indicates that the various facets of the crime can be identified only through custodial interrogation.

The petitioner's contention based on the reference in the FI Statement, though impressive on first blush, on a detailed analysis it is evident that the same is not material for the purpose of considering the nature of allegations raised against the petitioner.
8. Having regard to the nature of allegations, this Court is of the view that only custodial interrogation will be able to reveal the truth of the allegations.

In a recent decision in P. Krishna Mohan Reddy 2025:KER:40997 vs. The State of Andhra Pradesh (2025 LiveLaw SC 598) the Supreme Court had observed that custodial interrogation is qualitatively more elicitation oriented than questioning a suspect who is well ensconced with a favourable order of pre-arrest bail.

entities.text: P. Krishna Mohan Reddy 2025:KER:40997 vs. The State of Andhra Pradesh (2025 LiveLaw SC 598)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It was Adarsh A vs State Of Kerala on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128470968/
2 also observed that success in interrogation will elude if the suspected person knows that he is well protected and insulated by a prearrest bail order during the time he is interrogated.

entities.text: Adarsh A vs State Of Kerala
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In fact, the court went on to hold that insulating a person from arrest would make his interrogation a mere ritual.
9. Having regard to the circumstances arising in the case as well as the binding precedent referred to above, I am of the view that this is not a fit case to release the petitioner on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is dismissed.

Sd/-
